result: L. interrogans enters human and mouse vascular endothelial cells, renal tubular epithelial cells, and fibroblasts via caveolae/ITGB1-mediated, microfilament-dependent endocytosis involving PI3K or FAK signaling, forming membrane-bound Lep-vesicles. Maximum intracellular leptospiral numbers occur at 4 hr post-infection in most cell types, except mouse fibroblasts where numbers continue to increase.
evaluation: Claims C25-C41 provide converging evidence from pharmacological inhibitors (filipin, RGDS, Cyto-D, LY294002, 14/Y15), siRNA depletion (CAV1, ITGB1), and microscopy (Figure 1) demonstrating the specific endocytic pathway. The differential kinase usage (PI3K vs FAK) between cell types is experimentally supported, though the mechanistic basis for this difference remains speculative (C100).

result: Lep-vesicles do not fuse with lysosomes during infection, and leptospiral infection does not significantly alter expression of endocytosis/exocytosis-associated or lysosomal proteins.
evaluation: Claims C42-C45 are supported by confocal microscopy showing no co-localization with LAMP1 (Figure 2A) and Western blot analysis showing no significant changes in protein expression (Figure 2B). This is consistent with caveolae-mediated endocytosis avoiding lysosomal fusion (C13).

result: Lep-vesicles sequentially recruit Rab5 to form early endosomes (maximum 86.7-95.3% co-localization at 1-2 hr) and then Rab11/TfR to form recycling endosomes (maximum 75.2-90.3% co-localization at 4 hr). Fluorescence intensity decreases in most cell types during late infection but continues to increase in mouse fibroblasts.
evaluation: Claims C46-C50 are well-supported by time-course confocal microscopy with quantification of co-localization percentages and fluorescence intensity (Figure 3). The differential behavior of mouse fibroblasts is consistently observed and quantified, suggesting cell-type-specific differences in leptospiral trafficking.

result: Lep-vesicle-recycling endosomes recruit exocyst complex proteins Sec15 and Sec3 (maximum 73.7-84.2% and 69.2-81.9% co-localization at 8-12 hr). Treatment with anthrax toxin components (LF+PA or EF+PA) that inhibit Sec15 or Rab11 prevents complex formation without affecting leptospiral uptake.
evaluation: Claims C51-C60 are supported by confocal microscopy showing co-localization (Figure 4A-F) and pharmacological validation using anthrax toxin components (Figure 4G-H). The specificity of the inhibitors for blocking complex formation but not uptake strengthens the conclusion that exocyst recruitment is a post-endocytic event.

result: Lep-vesicle-recycling endosome-exocyst complexes recruit SNARE proteins VAMP2 and SYN1 (maximum 71.8-87.1% and 68.1-87.9% co-localization at 12 hr), forming ring-like structures at the cytomembrane. Transfection with botulinum toxin light chains (BoNT/D-LC or BoNT/C-LC) that cleave VAMP2 or SYN1 prevents complex formation without affecting uptake.
evaluation: Claims C61-C69 are supported by confocal microscopy (Figure 5A-F) and genetic validation using botulinum toxin light chains (Figure 5G-H, Figure 5—figure supplement 2). The ring-like localization at the cytomembrane (C64) provides morphological evidence for pre-exocytic positioning. Controls showing no cross-effects between BoNT/D-LC and SYN1 or BoNT/C-LC and VAMP2 (C68) strengthen specificity.

result: Intracellular leptospires are released from infected cells via FAK-MF/MT-dependent exocytosis mediated by endocytic recycling and vesicular transport systems. Release is prevented by depletion of Rab11, Sec15, Sec3, VAMP2, or SYN1, or by inhibition of MF, MT, or FAK (but not PI3K). Mouse fibroblasts release significantly more leptospires and show persistent intracellular propagation.
evaluation: Claims C70-C79 are supported by quantitative enumeration of released leptospires (Figure 6A-B) and confocal microscopy (Figure 6C-F). The differential requirement for FAK (but not PI3K) in exocytosis versus endocytosis is experimentally demonstrated. The unique propagation in mouse fibroblasts (C79) is consistently observed across multiple assays.

result: Both released leptospires and infected cells maintain viability during infection. Released leptospires show 93.1-96.2% viability, similar to cultured bacteria, with no significant difference in growth ability.
evaluation: Claims C80-C83 are supported by LIVE/DEAD staining (Figure 7A-B), growth curves (Figure 7C), MTT assays, and flow cytometry (Figure 7D-E). The maintenance of both bacterial and host cell viability distinguishes this from cytotoxic infections and supports the transcytosis model.

result: L. interrogans rapidly migrates through cell monolayers (maximum 47.1-53.3% transcytosis) without disrupting monolayer integrity, as evidenced by TEER values >200 Ω/cm² and FITC-dextran permeability <16.8%.
evaluation: Claims C84-C88 are supported by transwell assays with confocal microscopy (Figure 8A-B) and quantitative TEER and permeability measurements (Figure 8C-D). The maintenance of barrier function during transcytosis is well-documented and supports transcellular rather than paracellular migration.

result: Transcytosis through cell monolayers is mediated by endocytic recycling and vesicular transport systems. Depletion of Rab11, Sec15, Sec3, VAMP2, or SYN1, or treatment with filipin, RGDS, LF+PA, or BoNT/D-LC significantly reduces transcytosis while maintaining monolayer integrity (TEER >200 Ω/cm²).
evaluation: Claims C89-C95 are supported by transwell assays with various interventions (Figure 9A-C) and TEER measurements (Figure 9—figure supplement 1A-C). The specificity of effects—reduced transcytosis without compromising barrier integrity—strongly supports the proposed mechanism. Treatments that disrupt monolayer integrity (LY294002, 14/Y15, Cyto-D, COL, EF+PA, BoNT/C-LC) appropriately reduce TEER below threshold (C94).

result: L. interrogans invades endothelial and epithelial cells via caveolae/ITGB1-PI3K-mediated endocytosis but invades fibroblasts via caveolae/ITGB1-FAK-mediated endocytosis. This differential kinase usage may reflect cell-type-specific differences.
evaluation: Claims C96-C100 summarize the endocytosis findings with appropriate citations to prior work on E. coli (PI3K) and S. typhimurium (FAK) (C98-C99). The speculation about cell-type differences (C100) is reasonable but remains mechanistically unexplored. The experimental evidence for differential kinase usage is strong (C38-C39, C73-C74).

result: Lep-vesicles utilize endocytic recycling and vesicular transport system proteins to form sequential complexes for FAK-mediated MF/MT-dependent exocytosis. Rab11, Sec15, and VAMP2 recruitment are key steps, and the pathway avoids lysosomal fusion.
evaluation: Claims C108-C114 synthesize the mechanistic findings with appropriate integration of prior knowledge about VAMP2/SYN1 transmembrane domains (C109). The identification of key recruitment steps (C110) is supported by the loss-of-function experiments. This represents a comprehensive mechanistic model.

result: L. interrogans strain Lai rapidly migrates through human or mouse vascular endothelial, renal tubular epithelial, and fibroblast monolayers via caveolae/ITGB1-dependent endocytic recycling and vesicular transport systems.
evaluation: Claims C118-C120 summarize the transcytosis findings from the Discussion section. These are well-supported by the experimental data (C84-C95) and represent the integration of endocytosis and exocytosis mechanisms into a complete transcytosis model.

result: Intracellular leptospiral propagation occurs only in mouse fibroblasts, which release significantly more bacteria than other cell types. Both bacteria and host cells maintain viability, suggesting this mechanism may enable persistent urinary excretion in rodent hosts.
evaluation: Claims C124-C126, C128 are supported by quantitative data (Figure 6, Figure 7) showing differential behavior of mouse fibroblasts. The speculation about persistent excretion (C128) is reasonable given the data but represents an extrapolation from in vitro to in vivo that requires validation.

result: L. interrogans enters cells by caveolae/ITGB1-PI3K/FAK-mediated microfilament-dependent endocytosis, forming Lep-vesicles that avoid lysosomes and recruit Rab5/Rab11 and Sec/Exo-SNARE proteins for FAK-mediated microfilament/microtubule-dependent exocytosis. This transcytosis mechanism enables spreading in vivo and transmission of leptospirosis.
evaluation: Claims C129-C136 represent the main conclusions stated in the Abstract and Discussion. These are well-supported by the comprehensive experimental data presented throughout the manuscript. The in vivo relevance (C136) is a reasonable inference from the in vitro data but would benefit from animal model validation.

result: Background claims establishing leptospirosis as a global zoonotic disease, its transmission through contaminated water, pathogenesis involving septicemia and organ damage, and prior knowledge about endocytic pathways and bacterial internalization mechanisms.
evaluation: Claims C1-C24 provide established background knowledge supported by appropriate citations. These contextual claims are well-documented in the literature and provide the scientific foundation for the study. C12 references the authors' prior work on ITG involvement in leptospiral internalization.

result: Background claims about endocytic recycling and vesicular transport systems, prior studies on bacterial exocytosis and transcytosis, and leptospirosis pathogenesis in humans and animal hosts.
evaluation: Claims C101-C107, C109, C111-C112, C115-C117, C121-C123, C127 provide established knowledge from the literature with appropriate citations. These claims establish the conceptual framework for the study and identify gaps in knowledge (C117) that the current work addresses.
